content.comment_body: I'm experiencing the same issue with a deprecated platform. Everything worked fine a few weeks ago—I could control devices like the pool pump, lights, and timers using my phone. But since late August, I haven't been able to connect anymore. The only thing that still seemed to function was receiving the invoice (€25 for one month). I closed my AWS account, hoping to get new configuration instructions from [company_name] that are current.

It's unlikely that using cloud features with [product_name] is reliable in the long term, even for just a year or two. AWS isn't managed by [company_name], and Amazon can change the AWS API or its logic at any time. After a project that uses AWS is launched, you have to be ready for unexpected issues—for example, it worked until the end of August, and then it suddenly stopped. A better approach would be for [company_name] to offer its own cloud service for customers and guarantee long-term support for [product_name], perhaps ten years, so that cloud functionality works without interruption. The 'it works for me!' attitude in software isn't suitable for devices that need to operate for years without intervention. Remember WAP (Wireless Application Protocol)? Depending on AWS Cloud seems like setting yourself up for future problems. Ideally, [company_name] would move away from this cloud approach and instead offer features like e-mail, MQTT support for BM, or OpenVPN Client for communication modules. Adding Modbus/TCP to [product_name] was a helpful step for small system integrators. Cloud support is questionable…
A €25 annual fee would likely make [product_name] version [version_no] more popular. Just my opinion.
Regarding the invoice of €25 for one month—my calculations are different. Still, my main frustration is the lack of long-term reliability since AWS can change their API without notice. [url]

I don't understand all the [company_name] marketing about their integration with AWS. In every promotional video about the new [product_name] [version_no] cloud feature, they highlight this partnership. So it's confusing that they seem to ignore the issues we're facing right now.
Did you manage to solve your problem?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are reporting that cloud integration between [product_name] Web Editor and AWS stopped functioning reliably after a platform update or deprecation at the end of August, even though it had worked well before. The main concerns involve lack of long-term reliability, ongoing AWS costs, and limited official communication or updated setup instructions from [company_name]. Many question the wisdom of depending on third-party (AWS) platforms for essential device connectivity and suggest [company_name] should offer stronger, officially supported options for secure remote access.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and reliable cloud connectivity for their [product_name] systems, timely updates and clear guidance from [company_name] when platforms change, and an affordable cloud solution that fulfills the product's advertised capabilities.
